lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 我最近都在市场门口发呆，练级先欠着。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 修炼耐心，顺便等朋友上线。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 你那组标飞齿轮多少钱？

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 我刚刚连续砸爆三张卷。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 卷轴这东西，越想成越不成。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 我现在只想坐下冷静一分钟。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 先别点下一张，手抖会出事。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 你这身点装挺好看，哪里配的？

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 在时尚点装那边随便挑的。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 我也想换一套，站市场比较有排面。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 先试帽子，帽子决定气质。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 有的话喊我，我可以补位。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 缺主教，其他位置好像都有。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 今天市场人看起来多了不少。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 是啊，逛起来终于有点热闹了。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 刚刚还看到有人一直放技能。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 正常，站久了总得活动一下。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 去冰峰雪域是不是要从天空之城下塔？

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 对，一路往下走，记得带药。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 没掉，市场太舒服了就挂机了一下。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 你这是把市场当客厅了。

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 放心，这次应该只要二十分钟。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 以前射手村人真的很多。

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: 还有人为了名声吵半天。

# Town Presence — ambient social-bot population per town (v0.4).
#
# One entry per town. `maps` is the town's map family: the main town map plus any interior sub-maps
# (hospital, hideout, shops, salon). Each map carries its own fixed headcount so counts are hand-tunable
# (owner decision, 2026-07-07). Bots are placed by the anchor-weighted sampler (TownPresenceSampler):
# they cluster near NPCs/shops and on the main ground band, with a thin tail of stragglers on high
# ledges — no per-map coordinates needed.
#
# Level band sets the decorator tier/gear/job spread for that town's ambient crowd.
#
# `count` (per map) = STATIONED SocialBots that stand at anchor-weighted spots being social.
# `wanderers` (per town) = ROAMING TownWandererBots that stroll the town's map family, emote, and drift
#   between sub-maps. Henesys is intentionally absent — its hand-polished HenesysBots already cover it;
#   add a Henesys entry with a small `wanderers` only if you want a light top-up on top of them.
#
# To add an interior sub-map, append another `{map: <id>, count: <n>}` under that town's `maps:` —
# NPC-anchored placement is near-perfect in interiors since the NPCs define the room. 2–4 bots make a
# small room look lived-in. Seeded with main town maps only; interiors are added during curation.
#
# CURATION OVERRIDES (optional, per map) — the algorithm is the floor; these are the hand-polish on top.
# Switch a map from the compact `{map, count}` form to a block and add any of:
#   pins:  [{x: 1200, y: 200}, ...]                 # exact spots, always placed first
#   ban:   [{x1: 3000, x2: 4000}, ...]              # never place here (y1/y2 optional = full height)
#   boost: [{x1: 900, x2: 1600, mult: 2.5}, ...]    # multiply the crowd weight in this band
# The in-game `!env townpresence mark [mapId]` command appends pins to the machine-owned TownPins.txt
# sidecar (so this file's comments stay intact); those merge in automatically.
#
# After editing, apply live with `!env townpresence reload` (no server restart needed).

    maps:

      #   ban:  [{x1: 3200, x2: 4200}]   # e.g. keep bots off the far crane platform

soloMapling/server/EventMessageSystem/_E.text:
Start to end Flow

1. Event occurs in game
    a. A player gets a rare item from gachapon/levels up/scrolls pass or fail
    b. The game server creates a GachaponEvent with all relevant data (timestamp, player info, item, location)

2. Event published to Event Bus
    a. The event gets sent to the central EventBus
    b. EventBus looks up all subscribers registered for GACHAPON event type

3. Event Bus notifies each subscriber
    For each of the GachaBots:
        EventBus calls their onEvent() method with the event
        This happens immediately, no waiting

4. Each subscriber filters locally to see if the event matches their filter options

5. Bot Personal Queue
    a. The valid bots have local queues that contains the event
    b. More events might arrive in FIFO order

6. Bot State Machine
    a. when the bot's state machine finally does an event processing state
    b. will check queued events

7. Bot Processes Event
    a. Bot processess event in FIFO order from personal queue
    b. pops event off queue
    c. checks more events and processes those

8. Once queue is empty, bot continues it's task

Key Points
    Immediate delivery: Events are pushed to bots instantly via pub-sub pattern
    Deferred processing: Bots buffer events until they're ready
    Local filtering: Each bot decides if an event is relevant
    Ordered processing: Each bot processes its queued events in order
    Event Bus: Bots don't check for new events - they're pushed to them
